visibilityRules.note: Doctrine says rain, dust, mist, haze and fog reduce the effectiveness of night vision devices (IBB p201) but gives no figures; the caps below are my proposal. The grid is NOAA GSOD, 2016-2025, 174 stations, on the climate grid (5 arc-minutes); read it as what the nearest airport sees. GSOD gives a DAILY MEAN view, so it understates short fog episodes; haze is a proxy (a view of 3 km or less on a day with no fog, rain, snow, hail or thunder flag, so it also catches dust and smoke). An ordinary day on the plains has a mean view of 4-5 km, which is why the proxy uses 3 km, not 5.

surfaceBlockers.note: What stands in a line of sight that the 30 m elevation model (Copernicus GLO-30, a surface model) cannot show. aboveDsmM = its height above the model (the model already holds part of a canopy or a roof line); share = the chance that a line through one patch of it is blocked; ownShare = the chance that a man standing in it is hidden by it (the same as share when not given); grainM = the size of one patch of it (a field, a clump), so that a line crossing several cells of one patch counts it once. The lens works out the CHANCE that a line is clear: nothing is random and nothing is certain, so the cards say 'may be seen' and 'check on the ground'. Buildings use the bundle's building layer instead of a class (built). Tall crops use cropCalendar. Every figure carries its backing (basis, why, refs checked by tools/doctrine-refs/verify.py); where no book or data set gives it, the figure is a dated decision (E): the earlier figure is kept unless the evidence shows it wrong. Screening cuts both ways (less of it overstates fields of fire and fire coverage, more of it overstates concealment), so a decision is not moved toward either side without evidence; and the cards never say 'hidden' or 'safe'.

built.note: By the building layer's classes (rules.json grotbc.layers.bld; tools/terrain-pipeline/scripts/buildings.py). A line of length L through buildings scattered at density n, each w wide, meets one with chance 1 - exp(-n w L).
built.heightNote: height classes: not known or under 3 m, 3-6 m, 6-12 m, 12 m and over; half the class's median GHSL height is taken to stand above the 30 m model

model.why: The count of buildings a line passes is ITU-R P.1410's: sqrt(alpha beta) per km, with alpha the share of land under buildings and beta the buildings per km2; with alpha = n w^2 and beta = n that is n w per km, so n w L over L. Turning the count into a chance, exp(-n w L) of meeting none, takes the buildings as placed independently of the line (M; ITU spaces them evenly). w is the side of a square of the mean footprint, not its mean width across a line (4/pi of the side), so a line is never counted blocked by more building than the footprints show.

cropCalendar.basis: per crop, in its backing: S (FAO 56 heights and stage lengths; published heights of raya), data (crop areas 2023-24, FAO crop calendar, maize sowing windows), E (the two thresholds and the month rule); 2026-11-17, replacing the proposal of 2026-11-10
cropCalendar.note: Which crops on the cropland of Punjab and Sindh stand tall enough to screen, and when. tall = a crop whose maximum height is 2 m or more; hides = 1.2 m or more. A crop is listed in a month when, on the 15th, every planting in its calendar window has reached full height (the end of the development stage, FAO 56 Table 11) and none has yet been cut. share = the crop's area over the net area sown. Wheat and rice (1 m, FAO 56) reach neither threshold. Never raise concealment from this table alone: it only says how much of the cropland may screen in a month.

tallM.why: A crop counts as tall only when it stands over a standing man (the sight engine looks for a man of 1.7 m): its maximum height must be 2 m or more. A crop under that (cotton at 1.2-1.5 m) does not stand over a standing man's eye (1.6 m), so it does not screen a line between two standing men. The books name standing crops as cover from view but give no height; FM 5-33 calls grass over 1 m tall, a lower bar made for movement, not sight.

threatSets.note: What 'the enemy' brings when the planner picks a type of threat on the threat axis. Weapons are Symbols.json keys, so their ranges are the ones in the `Rng` field. The lens uses `max` (what can reach you).

effects.note: The judgement rules behind the OCOKA card: what each aspect means for the task, the test the lens computes, and where the rule comes from. The thresholds are the doctrine figures above; where a rule combines them the basis is E. The card gives a reason and a nearest better place, never a score.

rows.test: share of ground seen from 2 m above the point within 5 km >= 30 percent (the same test as the ITG reason O)
rows.src: IBB p282 s54.3 (maximum observation while denying it to the enemy); rules.json grotbc.itg.reasons.O

rows.test: the same viewshed read the other way: the point may be seen from the enemy's ground and from the high ground round it
clear line of sight toward the threat of 200 m or more (minimum for a primary task), 270-500 m desirable, below 100 m poor
clear sight against the weapon's own `eff` range from Symbols.json: say how much of the weapon's range the ground wastes
rows.src: IBB p38 (RR 2000 m direct) read with IBB p145-146 (country classes)

rows.test: dead ground inside the weapon's eff range in front of the position; it must be covered by another weapon or by obstacles and patrols
rows.src: IC s23.3; IBB p40 s8.2c (dead ground of one rifle covered by another)

rows.test: never trade cover and concealment for fields of fire: warn when fields of fire are good and concealment or cover is poor
masked from the enemy observer by undulating ground, woods or buildings; check against NVD range for the light and the visibility of the month
rows.src: IC s23.1e, s23.2a, s23.2e; IBB p201

rows.test: cover from indirect fire: troops in dead ground are safe from observed fire, not from indirect fire; the enemy plans fire on dead ground
an obstacle (canal, ditch, wet or soft ground, wire, minefield) in front of the position, inside the weapon's eff range and in clear sight, so it is covered by fire

rows.test: an obstacle slows or channels, it does not stop: name the crossings (bridges, fords, cuts in the bank, banks 6-9 m deep that can be cut) and the enemy's bridging means
classify the ground as unrestricted / restricted / severely restricted from GO / SLOW-GO / NO-GO for the mover, dry and after rain

rows.test: ITG candidates within reach, ranked by the reasons H O R P C J, with what each controls; designation (ITG, MITG) is the commander's
rows.src: NPS (key and decisive terrain); rules.json grotbc.itg

rows.test: ground 300-500 m ahead that gives extra range by day (mask position) and is out of the enemy's observation
a corridor of GO ground at least as wide as the echelon's frontage (frontage table), with the width, the NO-GO crossings and the tankable bridges on it
rows.src: FM533 ch 6 (avenue of approach: ease of movement plus dispersion for a force large enough); IBB Annex U

rows.test: where armour can come (tankable GO or SLOW-GO ground, class 60+ routes), the layout is built on tank-defeating defences first: anti-tank weapons and obstacles have priority
forming-up place and base of fire at least 1000-1200 m from the objective to stay out of enemy NVD range; tank base of fire inside the 800 m night firing range
country class from the viewshed: close (400-500 m or less) or very close (100-200 m or less) means the infantry leads and the enemy can use short-range anti-tank weapons
a crest between the position and the enemy that the defender can control by fire from flanking features; say what is lost: observation and direct-fire range
how often the month is foggy, hazy or dusty at the place (NOAA GSOD grid) and what that does to observation and to night vision devices

threatAxis.note: Where the enemy is: an option the planner repositions on the map, not read from enemy symbols (user, 2026-11-10). By default the threat comes from the front.

modes.front: the threat bearing is the unit's front: groundGuide.footprint.bearingDeg (0 = north today), so the frontage and the threat agree
modes.fixed: a bearing set by dragging the handle on the map (stored apart from the footprint facing)
modes.allRound: all-round: judge every direction and report the worst, as the footprint's worst-of-4 / circle modes do

threatAxis.handle: a draggable arrow on the map at the symbol or at the area's centre; dragging its tip turns the bearing, dragging its body moves the origin; follows the symbol unless it has been moved
threatAxis.persist: with the plan, like the Gr Scope target
threatAxis.keepsToGrotbc: the GROTBC verdict and enforce mode do not read the threat axis

policy.wording: Say 'may be seen from' and 'check on the ground', never 'hidden' or 'safe', from elevation alone (30 m cells show tree tops and roofs, not 1-2 m bunds).
policy.enforce: Enforce mode stays on the GROTBC GO / NO-GO rule in the OCOKA lens. An OCOKA verdict is a judgement call and never blocks a placement.
policy.keys: GROTBC keeps its keys (G R O T B C K D S P H V and Esc). OCOKA uses others.
